subject: Clarifying subprocessors, TIA scope, and UK IDTA options for Hearthwell
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@hearthwellhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hearthwellhealth.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@hearthwellhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TIA / subprocessors / UK IDTA questions for Redwood

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — Hearthwell is excited about the latency profile and the on-prem connector option. Before we proceed with procurement, legal and security asked for a few clarifications so we can scope the TIA and our internal signoff:

- Can you provide the current subprocessor inventory (and which subprocessors access KVs or any key material)? We only need the list for US and EU processing at this stage.
- Do you have a documented approach to UK IDTA / UK Addendum? If Redwood accepts the UK Addendum or offers a UK-IDTA equivalent, please note the signing path.
- For TIAs/DTIAs: Hearthwell requires an evidence package for crypto custody (KMS/HSM attestations), retention/ingress logs, and prefix caching behavior (to confirm caching does not store PHI).
- Are there routing options to force onshore-only processing for specific projects? If so, what are the constraints and cost implications?

I attached our TIA template and a short subprocessor RFI. Please confirm a delivery timeline — legal would like the initial answers and evidence in one week if possible.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Miller
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Hearthwell Health
Att: Hearthwell_TIA_Template.pdf, Hearthwell_Subprocessor_RFI.xlsx

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TIA / subprocessors / UK IDTA questions for Redwood

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (Legal ops) and Ben (SE) to help with the inventory and the technical evidence.

High level timeline: we can provide an initial subprocessor CSV and a redacted KMS/HSM attestation within 3 business days; the fuller TIA evidence bundle (logs, retention matrices, cache behavior diagrams) we can assemble in 5–7 business days depending on scope. If Hearthwell needs an onshore-only routing (US-only), that's supported for Dedicated and Private, and we can scope a canary routing policy for Hosted by model/region — Ben will confirm constraints and cost.

Would you like us to open a shared Drive for evidence handoff and to create a concise mutual action plan?

— Logan

Subject: RE: TIA / subprocessors / UK IDTA questions for Redwood

Quick technical summary for the team and to include in the evidence package: 

- Subprocessors: attached CSV (redacted for public listing) includes infra providers, observability (metrics/logs), and optional third-party tokenizers. Column flags indicate whether each subprocessor has access to KV cache or key material.
- KMS/HSM: we use a mix of cloud KMS (AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs for dedicated/private installs) and an HSM-backed signer for hosted key signatures. We can provide SOC2/HSM vendor attestations and a redacted key rotation log.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache is TTL-limited, per-tenant namespaces, and we have a documented policy that prevents caching of registered PHI patterns. We'll include the cache flow diagram and the eval which demonstrates PHI redaction in caching.
- Routing: Hosted: region routing + fallback to nearest compatible model (cannot guarantee pure US-only on shared hosted without dedicated contract). Dedicated/Private: fully addressable via project-level routing (cost varies by reserved capacity).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Share the redacted subprocessor CSV with Hearthwell (done).
2) Upload KMS/HSM attestation and cache diagram to the Drive.
3) Draft a short MMP (mutual action plan) with dates for TIA deliverables.

I can join a 30-min call with Hearthwell engineering/legal to walk through the cache diagram and routing constraints — available Tue/Thu next week.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20261015.csv (contains redacted vendor rows)

— Ben

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@hearthwellhealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: TIA / subprocessors / UK IDTA questions for Redwood

Jordan — 

Thanks for your patience. We uploaded an initial evidence bundle to the shared Drive (link below) and populated answers in your TIA template where we could. A few important notes and open asks for legal: 

1) UK IDTA / UK Addendum: Redwood accepts the UK Addendum in our standard DPA for Dedicated and Private contracts; for Hosted customers we offer an addendum execution path through our legal team (we have precedent customers where we executed the UK Addendum). We cannot sign a substitute UK-IDTA unilaterally, but are open to negotiating minor language in the addendum if required.

2) Subprocessor access to keying material: the CSV flags show that only our HSM vendor and our cloud KMS account admin role have indirect access to key metadata; application-level secrets and tenant CMKs are not visible to third-party subprocessors. We will provide a redacted key administration activity log in the Drive.

3) Evidence gaps: Hearthwell requested raw ingress logs for a 90-day window. We can supply aggregated logs and a sampling of raw entries under an evidence NDA; full raw logs require an operational playbook to pull and sanitize. Please confirm the exact log fields you need.

4) Onshore-only routing: to guarantee US-only processing on hosted infrastructure we need a Dedicated capacity letter or a private deployment. We can, however, provide routing SLOs and a fallback policy in the MMP for short-term pilots.

Proposed timeline: evidence bundle v1 uploaded today; v2 (sanitized logs + key rotation extract) in 3 business days once we have confirmation from Hearthwell on the log fields.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Hearthwell/TIA-evidence

If that works, Logan/Ben/Naomi and I will coordinate the MMP and set a 30-min review call with Hearthwell legal.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Data Protection
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@hearthwellhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: TIA / subprocessors / UK IDTA questions for Redwood

Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround and the Drive upload. A couple of quick confirmations so we can close the legal checklist: 

- The UK Addendum execution path is acceptable; legal will provide redline requests if required but this is a pass at our level.
- For the raw ingress logs: we only need a 30-day sample with headers and timestamps to validate retention and redaction; the sample under evidence NDA works.
- For onshore routing: Hearthwell can proceed with a Dedicated pilot if Redwood's capacity team can confirm throughput and a projected monthly commit. Please advise next steps for a Dedicated capacity quote.

Let's lock a 30-min technical review on Thursday 10/21 at 10:00 AM PT to walk the cache behavior and key admin logs. If that time doesn't work, let us know alternate slots.

Thanks — Jordan
